content: Hi! How can I help you today with your SQL query?
I need to make a report that lists customer names and their order totals.
Sure! To clarify, do you want to see the total number of orders or the sum of order amounts for each customer?
Sum of order amounts per customer, please.

Great! Here's an example SQL query with comments:
```sql
SELECT c.name, SUM(o.amount) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id -- link customers to their orders
GROUP BY c.name; -- aggregate by customer name
```
What if I want to include customers who haven't placed any orders yet?

You'll want a LEFT JOIN to include those customers. Here's how:
```sql
SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id -- include all customers
GROUP BY c.name;
```
Can I also add their email addresses to the result?

Absolutely! Just add the email column to the SELECT and GROUP BY clauses:
```sql
SELECT c.name, c.email, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.name, c.email;
```
How about just showing customers who spent more than $500?

You can filter aggregated results using HAVING:
```sql
SELECT c.name, c.email, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.name, c.email
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) > 500;
```
What if I only want customers from California?

Assuming there's a 'state' column in the customers table:
```sql
SELECT c.name, c.email, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.state = 'CA' -- filter for California
GROUP BY c.name, c.email;
```
Can you sort the result by total_spent, highest first?

Certainly! Add an ORDER BY clause:
```sql
SELECT c.name, c.email, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.state = 'CA'
GROUP BY c.name, c.email
ORDER BY total_spent DESC; -- highest spenders first
```

You can limit the number of rows with LIMIT:
```sql
SELECT c.name, c.email, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.state = 'CA'
GROUP BY c.name, c.email
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
Thanks! Can I get an explanation of how LEFT JOIN works here?

Of course! LEFT JOIN ensures every customer appears in the result, even if they have no orders. For those with no matching order, order columns (like amount) are NULL, which we convert to 0 with COALESCE.
